title: The Persian line that warns every king | Folio 3 — The Honest Historian #Shorts
description:
Now, at this point, I want to pause and tell you something about Beyhaqi. Again and again in his book, he warns his readers about this world, and how quickly it turns. In one famous passage, he writes a line that every student of Persian prose knows. Let me say it in Persian, and then in English. Ahmaq marda ke del dar in jahan bandad, ke nemati bedahad va zesht baz setanad. Foolish is the man who binds his heart to this world, for it gives a blessing, and then takes it back in an ugly way. Beyhaqi wrote that about another man, on another day. But I cannot think of a better line for the two sons of Sultan Mahmud.

The full story: Folio 3: The Blind King Who Ruled Twice — on our channel and on every podcast app.
